plainEnglish.text: A citizen initiative that has the Marin Healthcare District levy a parcel tax for thirty years. plainEnglish.text: Levies a special tax on parcels in the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division, placed on the ballot by petition. The money may be used only for improvements to, and later maintenance of, the road within the Division.
plainEnglish.excerpt: The stated purposes for the funds raised by this special tax are for improvements, and then later for maintenance, of the road within the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division.

yes.text: A yes vote lets the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division levy the special tax beginning the first full fiscal year after the measure takes effect.

no.excerpt: If this Measure is approved by two-thirds of the votes cast on this special tax proposal, the Upper Bay Permanent Road Division will levy a special tax beginning the first full fiscal year after the effective date.

fiscal.text: $4,350 per improved parcel and $2,175 per unimproved parcel per year for the first ten years, then $455 per parcel per year adjusted each July 1 by the San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward Consumer Price Index. The tax stays in effect until repealed. Estimated revenue is about $456,750 annually.
fiscal.excerpt: During the first ten years of the special tax, the rate of the special tax shall be $4,350 per improved parcel per year and $2,175 per unimproved parcel per year. Thereafter, the rate of the special tax shall be $455 per parcel per year. After the tenth year, the rate of the special tax shall be adjusted on July 1 of each year based upon the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward for the previous calendar year. The special tax will remain in effect until repealed. The Upper Bay Permanent Road Division estimates revenue from the special tax will be approximately $456,750 annually.

Measure B - Ballot Title and Summary - Napa County (PDF)

plainEnglish.text: A citizen initiative that imposes a countywide one-half percent sales tax for 18 years. The money can be used only for wildfire preparedness, watershed protection, open space preservation, and related administrative costs, split 50% to Napa County and 50% to the Napa County Regional Park and Open Space District, which must give it out through competitive grants.
plainEnglish.excerpt:
Measure B would impose a countywide sales tax at the rate of one-half of one percent (1/2%).
The tax would apply throughout Napa County, including the cities, town and the unincorporated
areas of the county.

yes.text: A yes vote imposes a ½% sales tax, limits its use to wildfire preparedness, watershed protection, open space preservation and related administrative costs, and approves the related actions in the measure.
yes.excerpt:
A “YES” VOTE MEANS that you want to impose a ½% sales tax, limit the use of the those
proceeds to wildfire preparedness, watershed protection, open space preservation uses and
administrative expenditures related to the planning and implementation of the Measure, and
approve the related actions described above.

no.text: A no vote means you do not want to impose a ½% sales tax to fund these uses.
no.excerpt:
A “NO” VOTE MEANS that you do not want to impose a ½% sales tax to fund the above-
described uses.

fiscal.text: Raises the sales tax by one-half of one percent (1/2%) for eighteen (18) years, from April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2045, in all cities, the town and the unincorporated area.
fiscal.excerpt:
• The sales tax in the cities of American Canyon, Calistoga, Napa, St. Helena, Town of
Yountville and the unincorporated areas of Napa County would be increased by one-half
of one percent (1/2%) for eighteen (18) years, beginning on April 1, 2027, and ending on
March 31, 2045.

notes: Citizen initiative, simple majority (impartial analysis by County Counsel). Excerpts are copied from the pdf.js text of the PDFs, which keeps the PDF line breaks as newlines. The ballot title and summary PDF (40594) has a text layer but no revenue estimate; no revenue figure was found in the impartial analysis either. The Argument in Favor (46100, 6 pages), Argument Against (46099, 2 pages) and both rebuttals are scanned PDFs with no text layer. The Argument in Favor PDF opens with scanned 'Statement That Argument Is True and Correct' author forms; the scans were not OCRed in this run because the browser pane was too narrow to check OCR against the image, so argFor, argAgainst, supporters and opponents are left out.

plainEnglish.text: Authorizes a one-half percent (1/2%) sales tax in the City of St. Helena. It is a general tax, so the money goes into the City's general fund for any lawful City program, improvement or service, and it stays in effect until repealed by voters.
plainEnglish.excerpt: If approved by a majority of St. Helena voters, this Measure would authorize a one-half percent (1/2%) retail transactions and use (sales) tax within the City of St. Helena.

yes.text: A yes vote authorizes the 1/2% transactions and use (sales) tax.
yes.excerpt: A “yes” vote on Measure S will authorize the 1/2% transactions and use (sales) tax.

no.text: A no vote does not authorize the 1/2% transactions and use (sales) tax.
no.excerpt: A “no” vote on Measure S will not authorize the 1/2% transactions and use (sales) tax.

fiscal.text: A 1/2% sales tax, or an extra 50¢ per $100 purchased, estimated to provide an additional $2,000,000 a year in local funding.
fiscal.excerpt: A one-half percent (1/2%) rate equates to an extra 50¢ per $100 purchased. It is estimated that Measure S will provide an additional $2,000,000 in annual local funding that could be used for maintaining general City services such as 911 fire/public safety response, City infrastructure including repairing roads/potholes/sidewalks, reducing local wildfire risk by managing brush/other fuels, maintaining parks, and supporting local businesses.

notes: General tax, majority vote. Impartial analysis by City Attorney Ethan Walsh, posted as a web page on the city site (the Napa County page for Measure S only links to the city's Ballot 2026 Information page). The city's Measure S pages (Ballot 2026 Information, Measure S, Ballot Question, Full Text, Impartial Analysis, Public Notice) post no argument in favor or against and do not say whether any were filed (argument deadline was August 3, 2026), so argFor, argAgainst, supporters and opponents are left out. The '$2,000,000 annually until ended by voters' wording is in the ballot question page.

The only official Measure Y document posted is Town Council Resolution 26-4427 (adopted June 16, 2026), which contains the ballot question; the Napa County page links only to the town's notices page. No impartial analysis, arguments or rebuttals are posted on the town site (the resolution set an impartial analysis deadline of August 7, 2026 and argument deadline of August 14, 2026), so yes, no, argFor, argAgainst, supporters and opponents are left out. Excerpts keep the PDF line breaks as newlines. The input had no ballot question; it reads: "To fully utilize TOT and sales tax generated from visitors for public services, parks and recreation, police, and fire emergency programs, shall the appropriations limit set by Article 13B of the California Constitution be increased by $3,000,000 plus 1/4 of TOT revenues for the prior fiscal year, for each year for a four year period commencing FY 2027/2028? By approving this appropriation limit, no existing tax is increased and no new taxes are created."
